greek: Καὶ Μωυσῆς ἦν ποιμαίνων τὰ πρόβατα Ιοθορ τοῦ γαμβροῦ αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἱερέως Μαδιαμ καὶ ἤγαγεν τὰ πρόβατα ὑπὸ τὴν ἔρημον καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος Χωρηβ.
hint: Moses, tending Jethro's flock, leads it beyond the wilderness and comes to Mount Horeb.

notes.text: The mountain Horeb: the Hebrew has har hāʾĕlōhîm ḥōrēbâ, the mountain of God, to Horeb.
Under the wilderness, toward it: the Hebrew has ʾaḥar hammidbār, behind the wilderness.
εἰμί with a present participle: was tending, an ongoing state.

names.gloss: (Μωυσῆς, from Hebrew Mōšeh, which the Hebrew of 2:10 hears in māšâ, "to draw out")
(Ιοθορ, from Hebrew Yitrô, usually connected with yeter, "abundance")
(Μαδιαμ, from Hebrew Midyān, of uncertain meaning)
(Χωρηβ, from Hebrew Ḥōrēb, usually connected with ḥārēb, "to be dry, waste")

greek: ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς ἐκ τοῦ βάτου, καὶ ὁρᾷ ὅτι ὁ βάτος καίεται πυρί, ὁ δὲ βάτος οὐ κατεκαίετο.
hint: An angel of the Lord appears to Moses in flame from a bush; the bush burns but is not consumed.

notes.lemma: ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς ἐκ τοῦ βάτου
notes.text: In a flame of fire out of the bramble-bush: Acts 7:30 quotes it, ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς βάτου.
βάτος, a bramble-bush, masculine here, for the Hebrew sĕneh.
The imperfect: it was not being burned up, as the burning went on.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Μωυσῆς Παρελθὼν ὄψομαι τὸ ὅραμα τὸ μέγα τοῦτο, τί ὅτι οὐ κατακαίεται ὁ βάτος.
hint: Moses decides to turn aside and see the great sight, why the bush is not burnt up.

notes.text: παρέρχομαι, to go by, aside: having turned aside.
Why is it that: τί as an adverb, as at 1:18.

greek: ὡς δὲ εἶδεν κύριος ὅτι προσάγει ἰδεῖν, ἐκάλεσεν αὐτὸν κύριος ἐκ τοῦ βάτου λέγων Μωυσῆ, Μωυσῆ. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Τί ἐστιν;
hint: When the Lord sees Moses approach, he calls him from the bush by name, twice, and Moses answers.

notes.text: κύριος without the article, as the Greek names God by the word for lord, for the Hebrew name YHWH.
προσάγω, to bring to, used without object: he draws near. Middle Liddell gives the intransitive, to draw near, last; the corpus's chain stops before it (see reference/open-questions.md, Q1).
What is it? The Hebrew has hinnēnî, here I am.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Μὴ ἐγγίσῃς ὧδε· λῦσαι τὸ ὑπόδημα ἐκ τῶν ποδῶν σου· ὁ γὰρ τόπος, ἐν ᾧ σὺ ἕστηκας, γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν.
hint: God tells Moses not to come near and to take off his sandals, for the place is holy ground.

notes.text: Aorist middle imperative of λύω: loose, for yourself; one form with the aorist active infinitive.
μή with the aorist subjunctive, a prohibition.

notes.lemma: ὁ γὰρ τόπος … γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν
notes.text: Acts 7:33 quotes it, with ἐφʼ ᾧ for ἐν ᾧ.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς τοῦ πατρός σου, θεὸς Αβρααμ καὶ θεὸς Ισαακ καὶ θεὸς Ιακωβ. ἀπέστρεψεν δὲ Μωυσῆς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ· εὐλαβεῖτο γὰρ κατεμβλέψαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
hint: God names himself the God of Moses' father and of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; Moses hides his face.

notes.text: θεός without the article three times after ὁ θεός: Mark 12:26 quotes the words with the article each time.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν Ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου τοῦ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ τῆς κραυγῆς αὐτῶν ἀκήκοα ἀπὸ τῶν ἐργοδιωκτῶν· οἶδα γὰρ τὴν ὀδύνην αὐτῶν·
hint: The Lord says he has seen his people's affliction in Egypt, heard their cry against the taskmasters, and knows their pain.

notes.text: Participle and verb of one root for the Hebrew infinitive absolute rāʾōh rāʾîtî. Acts 7:34 quotes the clause.
ἐργοδιώκτης, taskmaster: not in Middle Liddell; LSJ cites this verse, one translation, plain text.
ἀκούω with the genitive of what is heard.

greek: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ κραυγὴ τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ ἥκει πρός με, κἀγὼ ἑώρακα τὸν θλιμμόν, ὃν οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι θλίβουσιν αὐτούς.
hint: The cry of Israel's sons has reached God, and he has seen how the Egyptians oppress them.

notes.text: Noun and verb of one root: the pressing with which they press them. θλιμμός, not in Middle Liddell, is LSJ's = θλῖψις.
καί and ἐγώ in one word: and I.

hint: God promises to be with Moses: the sign is that, once out of Egypt, they will serve God on this mountain.

notes.lemma: ἐν τῷ ἐξαγαγεῖν σε … καὶ λατρεύσετε
notes.text: The time-clause, then καί opening the main clause, after the Hebrew wĕ-.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] to [[name:Μωυσεῖ]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] I will be [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of you, and [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] to you [[the sign|the sign, the mark and token, the sign from the gods and the omen, the signal, the standard and ensign, the boundary|σημεῖον]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] I you [[I send quite away|I send quite away, I dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]]; [[in the leading out|within, inside of, and by means of the leading out, the leading and carrying out from, the bringing forth into the world, the marching out, the ejecting, the carrying out and exporting, the drawing off, the calling forth and exciting, the leading on and tempting|ἐν; ἐξάγω]] you [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] of me [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]] and [[you will work for hire|you will work for hire and pay and be in servitude and serve, you will be bound and enslaved to, you will serve, you will obey, you will render due|λατρεύω]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only|θεός]] [[in the mountain|within, inside of, and by means of the mountain and hill|ἐν; ὄρος]] [[to this|to this, to the nearer, to what follows|οὗτος]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Μωυσῆς πρὸς τὸν θεόν Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐλεύσομαι πρὸς τοὺς υἱοὺς Ισραηλ καὶ ἐρῶ πρὸς αὐτούς Ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν ἀπέσταλκέν με πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐρωτήσουσίν με Τί ὄνομα αὐτῷ; τί ἐρῶ πρὸς αὐτούς;
hint: Moses asks what he should say when the Israelites ask the name of the God who sent him.

notes.text: What name to him: the dative of possession, with no verb.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] I [[I will come|I will come, I will go, I will go back and return, I will be going to and intend, I will come within a little of and be near|ἔρχομαι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] and [[I will say|I will say, I will speak, I will declare, I will call by name, I will tell|λέγω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] them [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[of the fathers|of the fathers, of the grandfathers|πατήρ]] of you [[has sent off|has sent off and it stands so, has sent away and banished and it stands so, has despatched and it stands so, has gone away and departed and it stands so|ἀποστέλλω]] me [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] you, [[they will ask|they will ask, they will ask about, they will enquire of and question, they will beg and solicit|ἐρωτάω]] me what [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] to him? what [[I will say|I will say, I will speak, I will declare, I will call by name, I will tell|λέγω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] them?

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Μωυσῆν Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν· καὶ εἶπεν Οὕτως ἐρεῖς τοῖς υἱοῖς Ισραηλ Ὁ ὢν ἀπέσταλκέν με πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
hint: God answers that he is 'the one who is', and that Moses is to say 'the one who is' has sent him.

notes.text: I am the one being: the present participle of εἰμί with the article, a name. The Hebrew has ʾehyeh ʾăšer ʾehyeh, I will be what I will be, and then ʾehyeh alone, which the Greek renders ὁ ὤν again.
εἰμί, to be, in the participle: the one who is, existing, not coming to be. Revelation 1:4 names God ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Μωυσῆν]] I am [[the one being|the one being, the one existing|εἰμί]]; and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[in this way|in this way, in this manner, so, thus, even so, so much|οὕτως]] [[you will say|you will say, you will speak, you will declare, you will call by name, you will tell|λέγω]] to the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[the one being|the one being, the one existing|εἰμί]] [[has sent off|has sent off and it stands so, has sent away and banished and it stands so, has despatched and it stands so, has gone away and departed and it stands so|ἀποστέλλω]] me [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] you.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς πάλιν πρὸς Μωυσῆν Οὕτως ἐρεῖς τοῖς υἱοῖς Ισραηλ Κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, θεὸς Αβρααμ καὶ θεὸς Ισαακ καὶ θεὸς Ιακωβ, ἀπέσταλκέν με πρὸς ὑμᾶς· τοῦτό μού ἐστιν ὄνομα αἰώνιον καὶ μνημόσυνον γενεῶν γενεαῖς.
hint: God gives Moses the name to tell Israel: the Lord, the God of their fathers, his name forever.

notes.text: Κύριος, lord, without the article, where the Hebrew writes the name YHWH.
Of generations to generations: the Hebrew lĕdōr dōr, to generation and generation.

[[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] of me is [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting and eternal|αἰώνιος]] and [[a remembrance|a remembrance and memorial and record, a memorandum and reminder|μνημόσυνον]] [[of races and stocks and families|of races and stocks and families, of breeds, of tribes and nations, of races and generations, of offsprings, of birth-places, of ages and times of life, of times of birth|γενεά]] [[to races and stocks and families|to races and stocks and families, to breeds, to tribes and nations, to races and generations, to offsprings, to birth-places, to ages and times of life, to times of birth|γενεά]].

greek: ἐλθὼν οὖν συνάγαγε τὴν γερουσίαν τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ καὶ ἐρεῖς πρὸς αὐτούς Κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν ὦπταί μοι, θεὸς Αβρααμ καὶ θεὸς Ισαακ καὶ θεὸς Ιακωβ, λέγων Ἐπισκοπῇ ἐπέσκεμμαι ὑμᾶς καὶ ὅσα συμβέβηκεν ὑμῖν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ,
hint: Moses is to gather Israel's elders and tell them the God of their fathers has appeared and has surely visited them.

notes.text: The dative of the noun with its own verb for the Hebrew infinitive absolute pāqōd pāqadtî, as at Genesis 50:24.
γερουσία, a council of elders, for the Hebrew ziqnê, the elders.
Perfect passive of ὁράω: has been seen by me, has appeared.

greek: καὶ εἶπον Ἀναβιβάσω ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κακώσεως τῶν Αἰγυπτίων εἰς τὴν γῆν τῶν Χαναναίων καὶ Χετταίων καὶ Αμορραίων καὶ Φερεζαίων καὶ Γεργεσαίων καὶ Ευαίων καὶ Ιεβουσαίων, εἰς γῆν ῥέουσαν γάλα καὶ μέλι.
hint: God has promised to bring them up from Egyptian oppression into the land of the Canaanites and the other peoples.

notes.text: And I said: the first person, God's words to Moses carried on.

reading: and [[I said|I said, I spoke, I declared, I called by name, I told|λέγω]] [[I will make go up|I will make go up and cause to mount, I will mount, I will draw up, I will bring up|ἀναβιβάζω]] you [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the ill-treatment|of the ill-treatment, of the distressing and harassing, of the neglect of parents, of the damage and misfortune|κάκωσις]] of the [[name:Αἰγυπτίων]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] of the [[name:Χαναναίων]] and of [[name:Χετταίων]] and of [[name:Αμορραίων]] and of [[name:Φερεζαίων]] and of [[name:Γεργεσαίων]] and of [[name:Ευαίων]] and of [[name:Ιεβουσαίων]], [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[earth|earth, land, ground|γῆ]] [[flowing|flowing and running and streaming and gushing, deriving its stream, flowing, running glibly, being current, falling and dropping off, melting away and perishing, being inclined and given|ῥέω]] milk and honey.

greek: καὶ εἰσακούσονταί σου τῆς φωνῆς· καὶ εἰσελεύσῃ σὺ καὶ ἡ γερουσία Ισραηλ πρὸς Φαραω βασιλέα Αἰγύπτου καὶ ἐρεῖς πρὸς αὐτόν Ὁ θεὸς τῶν Εβραίων προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς· πορευσώμεθα οὖν ὁδὸν τριῶν ἡμερῶν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον, ἵνα θύσωμεν τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν.
hint: The elders will listen; Moses and they are to ask Pharaoh for a three days' journey to sacrifice to their God.

notes.text: Has called us to him: the Hebrew has niqrâ ʿālênû, has met with us.
Aorist middle subjunctive of πορεύομαι, hortatory: let us go.

and [[you will go in|you will go in, you will go into and enter, you will come into, you will come in, you will come upon|εἰσέρχομαι]] you and [[the Council of Elders|the Council of Elders and Senate|γερουσία]] of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[a king|a king and chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]] and [[you will say|you will say, you will speak, you will declare, you will call by name, you will tell|λέγω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] him [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] of the [[name:Εβραίων]] [[has called to himself|has called to himself and it stands so, has called to one, has called to his aid, has cited|προσκαλέω]] us; names.gloss: (Εβραῖος, from Hebrew ʿIbrî, usually connected with ʿēber, "the region beyond")

greek: ἐγὼ δὲ οἶδα ὅτι οὐ προήσεται ὑμᾶς Φαραω βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου πορευθῆναι, ἐὰν μὴ μετὰ χειρὸς κραταιᾶς.
hint: God knows Pharaoh will not let them go unless forced by a mighty hand.

notes.text: Future middle of προΐημι, whose middle is to let go, give up; Middle Liddell keys it without the diaeresis.

reading: I [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[I know|I know, I am assured, I am versed in|οἶδα]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] not [[will send forward from himself|will send forward from himself and drive forward, will utter, will give up and let go and give up, will desert and abandon, will give away and give freely, will throw off, will throw away, will be lavish, will suffer, will suffer to escape, will give over and confide to his care, will neglect and disregard, will neglect all advice and be reckless|προΐημι]] you [[name:Φαραω]] [[a king|a king and chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]] [[to be driven|to be driven, to be carried, to go, to walk, to march, to go across and pass|πορεύομαι]], [[if haply|if haply, if|ἐάν]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of hand|of hand, of hand and arm, of arm|χείρ]] [[of strong|of strong and mighty and resistless|κραταιός]].

greek: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα πατάξω τοὺς Αἰγυπτίους ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς θαυμασίοις μου, οἷς ποιήσω ἐν αὐτοῖς, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξαποστελεῖ ὑμᾶς.
hint: God will stretch out his hand and strike Egypt with wonders, and then Pharaoh will send them out.

notes.text: θαυμάσιος, wonderful, with the article a noun: Middle Liddell's wonders, marvels.
The relative in the case of its antecedent, by attraction, for ἅ.

reading: and [[having stretched out|having stretched out, having spread out, having put forth|ἐκτείνω]] [[the hand|the hand, the hand and arm, the arm|χείρ]] [[I will beat|I will beat, I will knock, I will strike and smite, I will knock at|πατάσσω]] the [[name:Αἰγυπτίους]] [[in all|within, inside of, and by means of all, the whole, every, every single|ἐν; πᾶς]] [[to the wonders|to the wonders and marvels|θαυμάσιος]] of me, to which [[I will make|I will make, I will do, I will produce, I will create|ποιέω]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to them, and [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[will send quite away|will send quite away, will dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]] you.

greek: καὶ δώσω χάριν τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ ἐναντίον τῶν Αἰγυπτίων· ὅταν δὲ ἀποτρέχητε, οὐκ ἀπελεύσεσθε κενοί·
hint: God will give the people favour with the Egyptians, so they will not leave empty-handed.

notes.text: χάρις, outward grace, favour: for the Hebrew ḥēn.

reading: and [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] [[outward grace|outward grace, favour, loveliness, graciousness and kindness and goodwill, thankfulness and thanks and gratitude, a favour and kindness and boon, a gratification and delight|χάρις]] [[to the people|to the people, to the men, to the soldiers, to the land-army, to the common men, to the folk, to the Jews, to the Christians|λαός]] [[to this|to this, to the nearer, to what follows|οὗτος]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of and before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of the [[name:Αἰγυπτίων]]; [[whenever|whenever, until|ὅταν]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[you may run off|you may run off, you may run away, you may run hard|ἀποτρέχω]], not [[you will go away|you will go away, you will depart from, you will depart, you will depart from life|ἀπέρχομαι]] [[empty|empty and vain, to no purpose and in vain, void and destitute and bereft, empty-handed, empty of wit and empty-headed|κενός]];

greek: αἰτήσει γυνὴ παρὰ γείτονος καὶ συσκήνου αὐτῆς σκεύη ἀργυρᾶ καὶ χρυσᾶ καὶ ἱματισμόν, καὶ ἐπιθήσετε ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς θυγατέρας ὑμῶν καὶ σκυλεύσετε τοὺς Αἰγυπτίους. —
hint: Each woman will ask her neighbour for silver, gold and clothing to put on their children, and so they will plunder Egypt.

notes.text: Her neighbour and her tent-mate: the Hebrew has miššĕkentāh ûmiggārat bêtāh, from her neighbour and the sojourner of her house.
σκυλεύω, to strip a slain enemy, to despoil.
